title: Panel Layout
primary_metric: seconds of predicted task-completion time per successful actuation, across the full control sequence (accounting for expected extra attempts from each control's tested miss rate)

options.A: Recommend Close Reach — the larger Confirm control placed close to the resting hand position, at the cost of panel space the other required controls need
options.B: Recommend Long Reach — the smaller Confirm control placed farther from the resting hand position, freeing panel space for the other required controls

reinforcement_note: All four standards[] entries (calculus-critical-point, and the three how-to skills for finding/classifying critical points and solving an optimization problem) already sit at n=2 in standards_spine.json (covered_by The Curve's Turn and The Optimal Can) before this case. Checked every other Calculus/Applications-Of-Derivatives-adjacent skill in the spine for a genuine reach: Limits And Continuity, Integrals, Applications Of Integrals, and Series are all a different technique than this case's math forces (T(x) is built and differentiated with the constant/power/sum rule and log2, never integrated, and never needs a limit definition or a series expansion); the one uncovered skill in the Derivatives group, the quotient rule, is not forced either -- T(x) = (n+1)*a + b*log2(D_c(x)/W_c(x)+1) + n*b*log2(D_o(x)/w_o+1) differentiates via the chain rule on each log2 term (linear-over-linear inside the log, not a top-level quotient of two differentiated functions), so the quotient rule is not the technique a correct D1 solution actually uses. This case's real pedagogical reach is a second, independently-designed real-world optimization scenario (a closed-domain, physically-buildable allocation variable x with two named prototype endpoints) reinforcing the same critical-point/first-derivative-test/closed-domain-optimization sequence as its two siblings, not a padding remap onto an unforced skill.

sources.claim: Fitts's Law regression coefficients (intercept a, slope b) for the Shannon-formulation model MT = a + b*log2(D/W+1), 'touchpad + tap' condition, ISO 9241-9 conformant two-dimensional target-acquisition task
sources.units: a in seconds; b in seconds/bit
sources.title: A Fitts' Law Evaluation of Hands-Free and Hands-On Input on a Laptop Computer (Hassan, Magee & MacKenzie, HCII 2019, LNCS 11573, pp. 234-249)
sources.note: Real, dated, peer-reviewed ISO 9241-9 conformant study (paper explicitly ties its task to the ISO 9241-9 circular target layout and Shannon ID formula). Graded MEDIUM not HIGH: the measured task is a fingertip tap on a laptop touchpad, a proxy for this case's hand-reach-to-physical-button task. No public ISO 9241-9 study of a bedside medical-device control panel specifically was found. Author's mirror: https://www.yorku.ca/mack/hcii2019.html. CORRECTED at case-readiness Tier 2 probe 6 (2026-08-31, data-decay check): the DOI originally recorded (10.1007/978-3-030-49282-3_9) resolved to a different, unrelated 2020 paper by the same authors (LNCS 12188, HCII 2020); the correct DOI for this exact cited paper is 10.1007/978-3-030-23563-5_20 (LNCS 11573, not 11572). The numeric coefficients (a=0.6992s, b=0.1714s/bit, r=.9124) were independently re-verified against the author's own posted regression table at the mirror URL and are unchanged/confirmed correct.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Marcus Feld, Human Factors Engineer at Meridian Medical
content_sensitivity: Medical-device framing (SPEC §6). Kept strictly to the layout-optimization engineering decision — panel space, movement time, tested miss rate — never to an actual patient-harm incident. Routine engineering register throughout Overview/Background: the stakes are a tooling sign-off and a design-history-file finding, not a depicted clinical event. See FACILITATOR.md's Sensitivity note.

deliverables.text: The whole-panel Fitts's Law time model, built and differentiated: the Confirm control's width and distance, and the other required controls' shared distance, expressed as functions of a single allocation variable x (x=0 at Long Reach, x=1 at Close Reach), the resulting total predicted completion time T(x), its derivative T'(x) shown step by step, and the full algebra used to solve T'(x)=0 for every critical point in the feasible domain 0 <= x <= 1.

A first-derivative-test sign chart: the sign of T'(x) evaluated on each side of every critical point found in D1, each classified as a local minimum, local maximum, or neither, with a stated reason for each classification.

A closed-domain optimization table: T(x) evaluated at the domain's two endpoints (x=0 Long Reach, x=1 Close Reach) and at every interior critical point classified in D2, with the global minimum of T(x) on the feasible domain identified and justified by direct comparison, not asserted.

A miss-rate-weighted final decision table: using the panel's tested miss rates at Long Reach and Close Reach, and stating explicitly what is and is not known about miss rate at any interior time-minimizing layout, compute the expected seconds of predicted task-completion time per successful actuation (accounting for expected extra attempts from misses) for Long Reach, Close Reach, and D3's global minimizer, with a final recommendation stated in terms of that figure.

appendices.title: Panel Usability Test Log (Tested Miss Rates)

balance.argument_a: Close Reach gives the Confirm control a 30 mm target only 60 mm from the resting hand position (MA2, MA4), against Long Reach's 10 mm target 120 mm out (MA1, MA3) -- by Fitts's Law (a=0.6992s, b=0.1714s/bit, S1) that alone drops the Confirm control's own predicted movement time from about 1.333 s at Long Reach to about 0.971 s at Close Reach, and its tested miss rate from 6% to 1% (MA10, MA12). The Confirm control is reached every single pass through the sequence, so a roughly 0.36 s and 5-point-of-miss-rate advantage there compounds every time an operator runs it. If the 3 other required controls' movement time is not very sensitive to losing 60 mm of near-zone space (80 mm to 140 mm, MA5-MA6), Close Reach's per-use Confirm-control advantage could dominate the whole-sequence total -- the raw endpoint comparison alone (D3, before miss-rate weighting) shows Close Reach's T(1) approx 4.611 s already beats Long Reach's T(0) approx 4.625 s.
balance.argument_b: Long Reach keeps all 3 other required controls (MA8) at a shared 80 mm reach with an unpushed miss rate of 2% (MA5, MA11), instead of Close Reach's 140 mm reach and 7% miss rate for those same 3 controls (MA6, MA13) -- a smaller-looking per-control penalty at Close Reach, but multiplied by 3 and by the extra retries a 7% (versus 2%) miss rate forces, it outweighs the Confirm control's own roughly 0.36 s Close-Reach advantage. Computed for the whole sequence with Appendix C's tested miss rates folded in (D4): Long Reach's expected time per successful actuation is about 4.777 s versus Close Reach's about 4.894 s -- Long Reach wins by 2.46%, even though Close Reach wins on the Confirm control alone and even though Close Reach's raw (non-miss-rate-weighted) T(1) beats Long Reach's raw T(0).
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendix A's endpoint widths/distances, Appendix B's Fitts's Law coefficients, and Appendix C's tested miss rates are sourced, build T(x) (D1), find and classify its critical point(s) (D1-D2), compare T(x) at x=0, x=1, and the interior critical point (D3), then compute the miss-rate-weighted expected seconds per successful actuation at all three x values (D4) and compare directly.
balance.winner: B (Long Reach) wins on the primary metric -- expected seconds of predicted task-completion time per successful actuation, computed at the two named options; margin 2.46% over A (Close Reach). The raw (non-miss-rate-weighted) time-minimizing x* = 3/4 - sqrt(15)/12 ~= 0.4273 beats both named endpoints on movement time alone, but has no tested miss-rate figure (see D4/MA notes) so is not itself recommendable.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Below the ~20 mm range commonly associated with reliable, low-error touch/push actuation in human-factors usability literature -- consistent with Long Reach's narrative of a deliberately undersized Confirm control.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds MTc(0) in D1's model. Raising this value shrinks Long Reach's Confirm-control disadvantage. Load-bearing (HIGH, found at Tier 2 P5): a -50% flex (to 5mm) flips the D4 verdict to Close Reach -- see sensitivity_disclosure[].

modeling_assumptions.basis: Comfortably above the ~20 mm reliable-actuation range, consistent with Close Reach's narrative of a deliberately oversized Confirm control.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds MTc(1). Lowering this toward MA1's value flattens the trade-off and can remove the interior critical point entirely.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Outer edge of a plausible near-zone reach envelope (~50-150 mm from the resting hand position).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds MTc(0) and D3's endpoint comparison directly.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Inner portion of the same envelope, close to the resting hand position.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds MTc(1); a smaller value strengthens Close Reach's own-control advantage but does not change D4's outcome much, since the other controls dominate D4 (see MA13).

modeling_assumptions.basis: Inner portion of the envelope -- Long Reach's premise is that these controls stay close.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds MTo(0), multiplied by MA8's count -- the single most consequential distance figure for D4's Long Reach value. Load-bearing (HIGH, found at Tier 2 P5): a +50% flex (to 120mm) flips the D4 verdict to Close Reach -- see sensitivity_disclosure[].

modeling_assumptions.basis: Outer edge of the envelope -- Close Reach's premise is that these controls get pushed out.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing (HIGH). Feeds MTo(1). Close Reach only wins D4's final comparison if this value drops below approx. 118 mm, holding every other figure fixed -- verified numerically.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Fixed target width of each other required control
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set at the same ~20 mm reliable-actuation benchmark used for MA1/MA2, since these controls' size does not change with x.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds both MTo(0) and MTo(1) equally; shifts both options' other-control time similarly and does not by itself flip D4.

modeling_assumptions.basis: A short post-setup confirmation sequence on a bedside infusion console plausibly has a small number of required checks beyond Confirm (e.g. rate/target confirmation, an alarm-silence acknowledgment, a start acknowledgment); 3 is a mid-range, defensible count.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly dilemma-flipping (HIGH). At n=1 or n=2, Close Reach wins D4's expected-time comparison; at n=3 (used) or higher, Long Reach wins -- verified numerically for n=1..20.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Linear interpolation of width/distance in x between the two named endpoints
modeling_assumptions.value_used: (structural modeling choice, not a numeric value)
modeling_assumptions.basis: The simplest model consistent with a continuous range of buildable layouts between the only two prototypes actually tooled -- with no third prototype tested, a straight line is the least additional assumption a modeler can add.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: A non-linear interpolation could move x* without changing which of D3's compared values is largest, but this has not been checked numerically for this case.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Confirm control tested miss rate, Long Reach (x=0)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set higher than Close Reach's, consistent with a smaller, farther target; within the range usability testing commonly reports for a non-trivial but not extreme error rate under a small test-operator sample.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds D4's expected-attempts multiplier for the Confirm term at Long Reach; a lower value would make Long Reach's D4 win larger, not smaller.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Other-controls average tested miss rate, Long Reach (x=0)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set low, consistent with those controls sitting in the easiest, closest part of the near-zone at this option.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Small individual effect, multiplied by MA8's count of 3 in D4 -- MA6, MA8, and MA13 are the more consequential levers.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Confirm control tested miss rate, Close Reach (x=1)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set low, consistent with a large, close target.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Even setting this to 0 does not flip D4's result on its own -- verified numerically (threshold would be negative, i.e. unreachable). The case's real sensitivity lives in MA6/MA8/MA13, not here.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Other-controls average tested miss rate, Close Reach (x=1)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set higher than Long Reach's, consistent with those controls being pushed to the outer, more error-prone part of the near-zone at this option.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing (HIGH). Multiplied by MA8's count of 3 in D4. Close Reach only wins D4's final comparison if this value drops below approx. 4.1%, holding every other figure fixed -- verified numerically.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct = 2.46% (well under the ~20% retune threshold, not flagged). The result is genuinely close and driven by three assumed figures, not by the sourced Fitts's-law coefficients: MA8 (count of other required controls, flips between n=2 and n=3), MA6 (Close Reach other-controls distance, flips below ~118mm), and MA13 (Close Reach other-controls miss rate, flips below ~4.1%). All three MA are flagged HIGH sensitivity in modeling_assumptions[].

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Meridian Medical and this hardware revision are invented for this case (Appendix D); no real product's panel drawing exists to cite, so the Long Reach Confirm-control width is a documented good-faith estimate placed below the ~20mm reliable-actuation benchmark, not a measured figure -- flexing it -50% (to 5mm) is discovered by Tier 2 probe 5 to flip the verdict.

Invented device (Appendix D); the Long Reach other-controls distance is chosen within the plausible 50-150mm near-zone envelope, not measured from a real product -- flexing it +50% (to 120mm) is discovered by Tier 2 probe 5 to flip the verdict, a genuine instability alongside MA6/MA8/MA13.

Invented device (Appendix D); already flagged HIGH sensitivity and dilemma-flipping in modeling_assumptions[] -- mechanically verified flip threshold approx 118.07mm (case uses 140mm), reproduced in sensitivity_model.py.

Invented device (Appendix D); already flagged HIGH sensitivity and dilemma-flipping in modeling_assumptions[] -- mechanically verified continuous flip threshold approx n=2.365, i.e. flips between the integers n=2 and n=3 (case uses n=3), reproduced in sensitivity_model.py.

Invented device (Appendix D); already flagged HIGH sensitivity and dilemma-flipping in modeling_assumptions[] -- mechanically verified flip threshold approx 4.12% (case uses 7%), reproduced in sensitivity_model.py.

derived._note: T'(x)=0 reduces to 24x^2 - 36x + 11 = 0; x* = 3/4 - sqrt(15)/12. All figures verified in cases/the-panel-layout/sensitivity_model.py against case.md's D1-D4 model and case.json.balance.margin_pct.
